title: 08. GraphRAG: Graph Databases for Graph RAG
summary: Graph databases store, query, and traverse graph-structured data natively — unlike relational databases that require expensive JOIN operations for relationship traversal.

sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body: Graph databases store, query, and traverse graph-structured data natively — unlike relational databases that require expensive JOIN operations for relationship traversal. The core advantage for Graph RAG is that multi-hop traversal (A→B→C→D) is O(k) per hop in a graph DB vs O(n²) per JOIN in a relational DB. Key databases in the Graph RAG ecosystem: **Neo4j** (property graph, Cypher), **Amazon Neptune** (managed, SPARQL + Gremlin), **ArangoDB** (multi-model), **TigerGraph** (distributed analytics), **Memgraph** (in-memory, real-time), and **NetworkX** (Python, in-memory, prototyping). Selection criteria for production Graph RAG: query latency, vector index support, horizontal scalability, managed service availability, and team expertise.

sections.title: ④ Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
              GRAPH DATABASE SELECTION FOR GRAPH RAG

  DECISION TREE
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                                                        │
  │  < 1M nodes + latency < 100ms?                        │
  │         YES → MEMGRAPH (in-memory, sub-ms queries)    │
  │         NO  ↓                                         │
  │                                                        │
  │  AWS cloud + managed service required?                 │
  │         YES → AMAZON NEPTUNE (Gremlin or SPARQL)      │
  │         NO  ↓                                         │
  │                                                        │
  │  > 100M nodes + horizontal scale needed?               │
  │         YES → TIGERGRAPH (distributed analytics)      │
  │         NO  ↓                                         │
  │                                                        │
  │  Need built-in vector index + Cypher?                  │
  │         YES → NEO4J (best Graph RAG ecosystem)        │
  │         NO  ↓                                         │
  │                                                        │
  │  Need graph + document + full-text in one DB?          │
  │         YES → ARANGODB (multi-model)                  │
  │                                                        │
  │  Prototyping / research?                               │
  │         → NETWORKX (Python, in-memory, all algorithms)│
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  NEO4J GRAPH RAG ARCHITECTURE
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                                                        │
  │  Application Layer                                     │
  │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
  │  │  Graph RAG Query Engine                          │ │
  │  │  LangChain/LlamaIndex Integration                │ │
  │  └──────────┬───────────────────────────────────────┘ │
  │             │ Bolt Protocol (port 7687)               │
  │  ┌──────────▼───────────────────────────────────────┐ │
  │  │  Neo4j Connection Pool (max 50 connections)      │ │
  │  └──────────┬───────────────────────────────────────┘ │
  │             │                                         │
  │  ┌──────────▼───────────────────────────────────────┐ │
  │  │              NEO4J DATABASE                      │ │
  │  │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │
  │  │  │  VECTOR INDEX (entity embeddings)           │ │ │
  │  │  │  → Semantic similarity search               │ │ │
  │  │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │
  │  │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │
  │  │  │  GRAPH STORE (property graph)               │ │ │
  │  │  │  → Cypher traversal (2-hop, k-hop)          │ │ │
  │  │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │
  │  │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │
  │  │  │  GDS (Graph Data Science)                   │ │ │
  │  │  │  → PageRank, Leiden, Betweenness            │ │ │
  │  │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │
  │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
  │                                                        │
  │  Cache Layer                                           │
  │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
  │  │  Redis Graph Cache (TTL: 30 min)                 │ │
  │  │  → Subgraph cache by entity hash                │ │
  │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  QUERY LATENCY BENCHMARK (10M nodes, 50M edges)
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                                                        │
  │  Entity lookup by name:     Neo4j  5ms  Memgraph  1ms │
  │  1-hop traversal:           Neo4j 20ms  Memgraph  5ms │
  │  2-hop traversal:           Neo4j 80ms  Memgraph 20ms │
  │  3-hop traversal:           Neo4j 500ms Memgraph 100ms│
  │  Vector search (top-10):    Neo4j 30ms  (no native)   │
  │  Community detection (GDS): Neo4j 2min  (MAGE 30s)    │
  │                                                        │
  │  → 2-hop is the sweet spot for Graph RAG latency      │
  │  → Always add LIMIT to traversal queries              │
  │  → Cache k-hop results in Redis for repeated queries  │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Neo4j has: (1) native property graph storage with index-free adjacency (O(1) edge traversal), (2) native vector index for hybrid graph-vector search, (3) a rich…
quiz.explanation: Neo4j has: (1) native property graph storage with index-free adjacency (O(1) edge traversal), (2) native vector index for hybrid graph-vector search, (3) a rich algorithm library (PageRank, community detection, shortest paths) via GDS (Graph Data Science library), (4) APOC plugin for advanced procedures, (5) a Cypher query language that is SQL-like and readable, and (6) LangChain + LlamaIndex integrations.

quiz.question: What is Amazon Neptune and when would you choose it over Neo4j for Graph RAG?
options: NetworkX is a pure-Python in-memory graph library — NOT a database, but the most widely used tool for graph algorithm prototyping and small-to-medium graph processing.
Memgraph is an in-memory graph database with a Cypher-compatible API, designed for real-time streaming graph analytics.
S1. SCENARIO: Graph DB query takes 30 seconds for a 2-hop traversal on 10M nodes — index optimisation.
Neptune is AWS's fully managed graph database supporting both property graphs (Gremlin query language) and RDF (SPARQL).
quiz.explanation: Neptune is AWS's fully managed graph database supporting both property graphs (Gremlin query language) and RDF (SPARQL). Key advantages over Neo4j: managed service (no ops overhead), auto-scaling storage up to 64TB, native integration with AWS services (SageMaker, OpenSearch for vector search), multi-AZ HA.

quiz.question: What is ArangoDB's multi-model architecture and how does it benefit Graph RAG?
options: S1. SCENARIO: Graph DB query takes 30 seconds for a 2-hop traversal on 10M nodes — index optimisation.
Memgraph is an in-memory graph database with a Cypher-compatible API, designed for real-time streaming graph analytics.

quiz.explanation: documents** (JSON), graphs (property graph), and key-value pairs in a single engine with a unified query language (AQL — ArangoDB Query Language). This multi-model approach benefits Graph RAG because: (1) entities can be stored as JSON documents (flexible schema), (2) graph traversal is native, (3) full-text search is built-in (no separate search engine), (4) geospatial queries for location-aware Graph RAG.

options: S1. SCENARIO: Graph DB query takes 30 seconds for a 2-hop traversal on 10M nodes — index optimisation.
documents** (JSON), graphs (property graph), and key-value pairs in a single engine with a unified query language (AQL — ArangoDB Query Language).
NetworkX is a pure-Python in-memory graph library — NOT a database, but the most widely used tool for graph algorithm prototyping and small-to-medium graph processing.
Memgraph is an in-memory graph database with a Cypher-compatible API, designed for real-time streaming graph analytics.
quiz.explanation: Memgraph is an in-memory graph database with a Cypher-compatible API, designed for real-time streaming graph analytics. Key advantages: sub-millisecond query latency (everything in RAM), streaming integrations (Kafka, Pulsar), graph algorithm library (MAGE), and dynamic Cypher compatibility with Neo4j. Disadvantages: dataset size limited by RAM, no vector index out of the box.

quiz.explanation: NetworkX is a pure-Python in-memory graph library — NOT a database, but the most widely used tool for graph algorithm prototyping and small-to-medium graph processing. It supports all standard graph algorithms (BFS, DFS, PageRank, shortest paths, community detection via python-louvain), all graph types (directed, undirected, multi-graph), and integrates natively with NumPy/SciPy.
